test_case.description: Fault injection — simulate scheduler stall and verify watchdog latches the motor driver
test_case.setup: Pump in standard infusion mode; instrumented build with a debug hook to suspend the rate-control task indefinitely.
test_case.steps: 1. Start an infusion at 5 mL/hr. 2. Trigger the debug hook to suspend the rate-control task. 3. Observe the watchdog timer and motor driver state. 4. Observe the UI banner.
test_case.expectedResults: 1. Watchdog counter stalls as expected. 2. After 200 ms, the motor driver latches to the safe state and stops issuing pulses. 3. The UI renders the Alarm Mode banner and silences the nominal-rate display.

requirements.text: The rate-control loop shall be monitored by an independent hardware watchdog. The motor driver shall be latched into a safe (no-pulse) state if a heartbeat from the rate-control task is missed for more than 200 ms.
The UI thread shall render an Alarm Mode banner and silence nominal-rate displays when the rate-control task heartbeat is missed for more than 200 ms.

test_case.description: Verify MFA enforcement cannot be bypassed by direct URL navigation.
test_case.setup: EHR authentication service running; test user has valid credentials but has not completed MFA.
test_case.steps:
Step: 1. Complete first-factor authentication (password only).
Step: 2. Capture the session token from browser cookies.
Step: 3. Attempt to navigate directly to the EHR dashboard URL without completing MFA.
Step: 4. Observe the system response.
test_case.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. Password authentication succeeds and MFA prompt is displayed.
ExpectedResult: 2. Session token is captured but marked as 'MFA_PENDING'.
ExpectedResult: 3. System intercepts the direct navigation attempt.
ExpectedResult: 4. User is redirected back to the MFA prompt page with message 'Multi-factor authentication required'.

requirements.text: The EHR system shall enforce multi-factor authentication (MFA) for all users accessing patient health information (PHI), requiring both a password and a time-based one-time password (TOTP) token generated by an authenticator app.
The EHR system shall prevent unauthorized access to PHI by enforcing MFA completion before granting access to any PHI-containing routes, including direct URL navigation attempts.

test_case.description: Verify video quality does NOT restore to HD if bandwidth drops below 2.0 Mbps before 10-second stabilization period completes.
test_case.setup: Telemedicine video module active; video call in SD mode; network throttling tool configured.
test_case.steps:
Step: 1. Verify current video resolution is 640x480.
Step: 2. Increase bandwidth to 2.5 Mbps.
Step: 3. After 5 seconds, drop bandwidth to 1.8 Mbps.
Step: 4. Observe video stream quality.
test_case.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. Video resolution is 640x480.
ExpectedResult: 2. Bandwidth increases above 2.0 Mbps.
ExpectedResult: 3. Bandwidth drops below 2.0 Mbps before 10-second timer completes.
ExpectedResult: 4. Video stream remains in SD mode (640x480); no upgrade to HD occurs.

requirements.text: The telemedicine video consultation module shall automatically degrade the video stream quality from HD (1280x720) to SD (640x480) when the detected network bandwidth drops below 1.5 Mbps, and shall restore HD quality when bandwidth recovers above 2.0 Mbps for at least 10 consecutive seconds.
